problem_text:
A logistics manager needs to select cargo containers for shipment. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 36 m³, revenue $217
* Container 2: volume 34 m³, revenue $252
* Container 3: volume 11 m³, revenue $89
* Container 4: volume 1 m³, revenue $278
* Container 5: volume 30 m³, revenue $47
* Container 6: volume 27 m³, revenue $173
* Container 7: volume 47 m³, revenue $101
* Container 8: volume 6 m³, revenue $300
* Container 9: volume 50 m³, revenue $184
* Container 10: volume 30 m³, revenue $108
* Container 11: volume 46 m³, revenue $260
* Container 12: volume 44 m³, revenue $224
* Container 13: volume 4 m³, revenue $90
* Container 14: volume 17 m³, revenue $159
* Container 15: volume 35 m³, revenue $160
* Container 16: volume 43 m³, revenue $233
* Container 17: volume 50 m³, revenue $10
* Container 18: volume 42 m³, revenue $262
* Container 19: volume 5 m³, revenue $251
* Container 20: volume 19 m³, revenue $249
* Container 21: volume 44 m³, revenue $293
* Container 22: volume 24 m³, revenue $255
* Container 23: volume 40 m³, revenue $45
* Container 24: volume 42 m³, revenue $167
* Container 25: volume 14 m³, revenue $224

The cargo vessel has a maximum capacity of 518 m³. Choose the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully shipped or left behind.
